content: Treatment for cervical precancerous lesions is only provided if both the HPV test and visual inspection with acetic acid (VIA) yield positive results. If eligible for cryotherapy, the patient is treated with cryotherapy. If not eligible for cryotherapy, treatment is performed using loop electrosurgical excision procedure (LEEP). Post-treatment follow-up is conducted one year after the procedure. If VIA results are negative, rescreening is recommended every 3–5 years. If the results are suspicious for cancer, the patient is referred for appropriate diagnostic and treatment services. According to WHO guidelines, screening for cervical cancer prevention involves an HPV test followed by colposcopy, with or without biopsy. Treatment options include cryotherapy or LEEP for those not eligible for cryotherapy. Women with a positive colposcopic impression may undergo biopsy for histological confirmation or receive immediate treatment. If colposcopy is negative, rescreening is recommended after a minimum interval of five years. If biopsy confirms CIN 2 or higher, treatment with cryotherapy or LEEP is advised. For CIN 1 or less, rescreening within three years is recommended. For women with HIV-positive or unknown HIV status in areas with high endemic HIV infection, screening strategies involve HPV testing followed by VIA to determine eligibility for cryotherapy and to rule out cervical cancer. If the HPV test is positive, VIA is used as a secondary screening test to decide on treatment. Treatment is only offered if both HPV and VIA results are positive. If VIA is negative, rescreening is recommended within three years. If the patient is not eligible for cryotherapy, LEEP is performed. Suspicious findings for cancer warrant referral for further diagnosis and treatment. Screening with cytology (Pap testing) followed by colposcopy, with or without biopsy, is another approach. Women with ASCUS (atypical squamous cells of undetermined significance) or greater on cytology undergo colposcopy. If colposcopy is positive, rescreening is recommended within three years. If colposcopy is negative, rescreening is advised every 3–5 years. If biopsy confirms CIN 2 or higher, treatment with cryotherapy or LEEP is performed. For CIN 1 or less, rescreening within three years is recommended. The WHO guidelines emphasize the importance of referring to specific recommendations in Chapter 3 of the guidelines for guidance on preferred strategies and factors to consider when deciding on a screening and treatment approach. Detailed evidence and decision-making processes are outlined in supplemental materials.
